implementation_notes: JavaScript needs no framework base class: functions are the registration unit and the host runtime owns the loop that calls them - the browser dispatches to listeners added with addEventListener, Node's EventEmitter calls every listener synchronously when emit runs, and frameworks such as Express continue the pattern with middleware functions. The classic abstract class with hooks is replaced by a callback function registered with the owner of the flow, which is why callback-based APIs are the platform's default shape. The class form is still justified when the extension contract must be discoverable and shared by many consumers, or when a plugin implements several related hooks.
pitfalls: Listeners keep their closures alive as long as the emitter does; forgetting removeEventListener/off on long-lived targets leaks memory and leaves stale handlers firing.
emit calls listeners synchronously in registration order, so one throwing listener aborts the rest and a slow listener blocks the emitting code path.
